claims.text: The deviation is established and above tolerance on the platform's own recorded distances. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05006) gives actual_distance_km 14.6 and optimal_distance_km 12.7, so the deviation is 1.90 km, and POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km. Since 1.90 km exceeds 1.0 km, this case cannot be disposed of as 'within tolerance', and the excess distance fare route in the refund matrix is live.

The traffic data covering the recommended route does not justify the reroute. The LTA record for the AYE (towards City) between Clementi Rd and Keppel Viaduct (EV-ADVIS-05006-01) is the advisory that sits on the recommended segment, and its type is NONE, with speed bands 4-6 throughout and no incident, roadwork or closure. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure; NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 admits. The justification limb therefore fails on the very segment the driver left.

The roadwork advisory the driver might point to is not on the recommended route. EV-ADVIS-05006-02 is a ROADWORK on Pasir Panjang Road (towards Telok Blangah) near Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre, and Pasir Panjang Road appears only in the actual route via list (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, West Coast Highway, Pasir Panjang Road, Telok Blangah Road, Keppel Road, Wallich Street) and not in the recommended route via list (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street) carried on the same trip record (EV-TRIP-05006). The trip record's own event log shows the vehicle left the recommended route at the AYE / West Coast Highway exit at 18:05:06 and rejoined at Keppel Road / Telok Blangah Road at 18:20:12, so the deviation was taken before and independently of any Pasir Panjang Road segment. An advisory on a road the recommended route never uses cannot satisfy POL-RD-23's requirement of an advisory that intersects the recommended route, and it cannot retrofit justification onto a departure already made.

The driver's 'AYE jam' is an uncorroborated assertion, and POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The only data for the AYE in the trip window (EV-ADVIS-05006-01) records no incident, roadwork or closure and speed bands 4-6 throughout, which is flowing traffic, not congestion. The rider's own account at filing was that the AYE looked clear past the slip road, which is consistent with the LTA record and not with the driver's claim.

The rider's 'ok' does not save the driver's case, and I do not overstate this: I accept that the driver messaged before the deviation (EV-CHAT-05006, MSG-05006-003 sent 18:01:46, 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?') and the rider replied 'ok' (MSG-05006-004, sent 18:02:11), while the deviation was detected at 18:05:06. POL-RD-21 makes that acknowledgment relevant only to whether the deviation is 'agreed'. POL-RD-24 row (a) yields no refund only where the reroute is traffic-justified as well as notified and agreed; a rider's agreement to a detour that the traffic record does not support does not make the detour traffic-justified. The driver therefore cannot bring himself within row (a), and rows (b) and (c), which also presuppose a traffic-justified reroute, are equally unavailable.

This case fits POL-RD-24 row (d) exactly: the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation was 1.90 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance. The consequence the policy attaches is refund of the excess distance fare in full, computed as deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd without surge: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD (EV-FARE-05006). That is precisely the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the present refund is the correct figure and the driver's claim to have the 1.37 SGD returned to his earnings is not supported by the matrix.

The outcome the rider is entitled to is PARTIAL_REFUND: part of the trip's charge — the excess distance fare — is returned, which is how POL-RD-24's own note labels rows (b) and (d), and it leaves the rider not carrying the charge for a 1.90 km detour the traffic record does not support. On the alternative reading, the present state already has the 1.37 SGD refunded (EV-FARE-05006: payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.37), and POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative — it preserves the present payment state and never restores a charge — so a NO_ACTION outcome would likewise leave the refund in the rider's hands rather than return the money to the driver. Either way the rider should not bear the disputed charge.

Nothing in this record requires escalation, and the rider's refund should be made terminal rather than held. The contested amount is 1.37 SGD (EV-FARE-05006, EV-TRIP-05006), below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence (value_band AI_FINAL) and POL-GEN-22's higher bars do not engage; POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied, and in any event the deviation is 1.90 km; and every fact the refund matrix needs — the two recorded distances, the notification and the acknowledgment in the chat log, and the traffic data — is in the record, with each artifact I rely on assessed COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 and POL-GEN-02 have no missing or impaired fact to bite on. There is no open question here for a human reviewer to answer.

claims.text: The driver gave the rider notice of the deviation before the point of deviation, and the rider agreed. The chat log carries MSG-05006-003, sent by the driver at 18:01:46 — 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?' — read at 18:02:06, and the rider's reply MSG-05006-004 'ok' at 18:02:11, read by the driver at 18:02:35. The trip record places the first route_deviation_detected event at 18:05:06, and the driver-device trace still fixes the vehicle on the Ayer Rajah Expressway at 18:04:34, with the first West Coast Highway fix at 18:05:04. Under POL-RD-21 the acknowledgment in the chat log makes this an agreed deviation: the notification obligation the clause imposes was met before the deviation, not breached at it.

The rider's own account does not deny that notice was given; her complaint is only that the AYE 'looked clear to me' when they passed the slip road — an observation made from the slip road, that is at or after the 18:05:06 point of deviation, not at the moment the driver had to choose between staying on the expressway and taking West Coast Highway. The chat log shows four messages and no objection during the trip: the driver's contemporaneous in-writing report of the jam at 18:01:46, accepted in writing at 18:02:11. Nothing in the record contradicts the condition the driver reported at the time he had to act on it.

EV-ADVIS-05006-01 does not prove the AYE was flowing. Its type is NONE, and POL-RD-23's own admissible-type table places NONE outside the kinds that matter, so that artifact records the absence of an incident, a closure or a roadwork — it is not a congestion finding. No clause of this policy assigns any meaning to the speed-band figures the artifact carries, so those figures cannot be read as a finding that traffic was free-flowing. What POL-RD-23 excludes is a driver's bare assertion of traffic as justification; it does not convert a type-NONE record into affirmative evidence that the expressway was clear when the driver decided.

The traffic-justification question is not closed on this record. EV-ADVIS-05006-02 is a live ROADWORK — a 'closure' kind on POL-RD-23's admissible table — on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah near Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre, valid 09:00 to 23:00 on 18 August 2026 and so overlapping the trip window. The artifact's own derived facts leave justifies_reroute null and record the intersection with the recommended route as undetermined, to be decided by the Judge from its road, direction and location against the trip. POL-RD-23 turns on precisely that intersection, and the derived facts — which are the only licensed source for that comparison — do not determine it; the record therefore cannot establish that the reroute was not traffic-justified, which is the fact POL-RD-24's matrix rests on.

The case fits no row of POL-RD-24 cleanly. Rows (b) and (c) are excluded because the rider was informed and agreed, as the chat log shows. Row (a) — the only row written for an informed, agreeing rider — additionally requires the traffic justification to be established, and the advisories do not establish it. Rows (d) and (e) presuppose a settled finding that the reroute was not traffic-justified, which this record does not deliver. POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case which fits no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation where a fact a rule needs — here whether traffic justified the reroute — cannot be established. The interim SGD 1.37 should therefore be held for human review rather than confirmed against the driver. The driver does not dispute the measurement: 14.6 km minus 12.7 km is a 1.90 km deviation over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance; what is not established is the justification the refund turns on.

Confirming the full excess distance fare against the driver also overstates what the deviation cost the rider. The recommended route carried ERP of SGD 2.50 (EV-TRIP-05006, optimal_route_erp_sgd) while the trip actually charged ERP of SGD 1.50 (EV-FARE-05006, tolls_erp); on the route taken the rider was SGD 1.00 better off in tolls, so the net excess she bore was about SGD 0.37, not SGD 1.37. POL-RD-24's formula allows no set-off and the driver asks for none; the point goes to whether the interim recovery should be finalised on this record or held, as POL-RD-24's closing words and POL-GEN-26 direct, for a human reviewer.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver: I accept that you told the rider before the deviation and that she agreed. Your message MSG-05006-003, sent 18:01:46 ('Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?'), was read at 18:02:06 and answered 'ok' at 18:02:11, and the trip record (EV-TRIP-05006) places the departure from the recommended route at 18:05:06 — so under POL-RD-21 the rider was informed and the deviation was agreed. That does not decide the refund: POL-RD-24's matrix requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well, and it was not.

POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The LTA record for the segment you left — the AYE towards the City between Clementi Road and the Keppel Viaduct (EV-ADVIS-05006-01) — is type NONE, with no incident, roadwork or closure. A NONE record is not one of the kinds the policy admits, so it cannot support the 'jam' you reported; and I do not read the speed-band figures as an affirmative finding either way, because no clause gives them that meaning. The only roadwork in the window (EV-ADVIS-05006-02: ROADWORK on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah, 09:00-23:00) is on Pasir Panjang Road, which appears in your actual route but not in the recommended route via Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road and Wallich Street (both lists are on EV-TRIP-05006). Deciding that comparison against the trip's own route lists, the roadwork does not intersect the recommended route and cannot justify the departure. There is therefore no undetermined fact here: POL-GEN-26 is not engaged.

The case fits POL-RD-24 row (d) — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km. The recorded distances are 14.6 km actual against 12.7 km recommended (EV-TRIP-05006), a 1.90 km deviation, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The excess distance fare is 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km (EV-FARE-05006) = 1.37 SGD, without surge. That is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from your earnings, so your request to have the 1.37 SGD returned to your earnings is not supported, and the interim adjustment is confirmed. I also reject the suggested set-off between the recommended route's ERP of 2.50 SGD and the 1.50 SGD actually charged: POL-RD-24 fixes the excess distance fare as deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge, and allows no set-off.

To the rider: the 1.37 SGD refund issued to you stands; the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND, because part of the trip's charge is returned and not the whole fare. The contested amount is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and this ruling is given at 0.90 confidence, above the 0.80 that POL-RD-25 requires for a route deviation. Each artifact this ruling rests on (EV-TRIP-05006, EV-FARE-05006, EV-ADVIS-05006-01 and -02, EV-CHAT-05006) is assessed COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so nothing is impaired and no escalation or referral follows.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established and above tolerance on the platform's own recorded distances. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05006) gives actual_distance_km 14.6 and optimal_distance_km 12.7, so the deviation is 1.90 km, and POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km. Since 1.90 km exceeds 1.0 km, this case cannot be disposed of as 'within tolerance', and the excess distance fare route in the refund matrix is live.

The traffic data covering the recommended route does not justify the reroute. The LTA record for the AYE (towards City) between Clementi Rd and Keppel Viaduct (EV-ADVIS-05006-01) is the advisory that sits on the recommended segment, and its type is NONE, with speed bands 4-6 throughout and no incident, roadwork or closure. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure; NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 admits. The justification limb therefore fails on the very segment the driver left.

The roadwork advisory the driver might point to is not on the recommended route. EV-ADVIS-05006-02 is a ROADWORK on Pasir Panjang Road (towards Telok Blangah) near Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre, and Pasir Panjang Road appears only in the actual route via list (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, West Coast Highway, Pasir Panjang Road, Telok Blangah Road, Keppel Road, Wallich Street) and not in the recommended route via list (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street) carried on the same trip record (EV-TRIP-05006). The trip record's own event log shows the vehicle left the recommended route at the AYE / West Coast Highway exit at 18:05:06 and rejoined at Keppel Road / Telok Blangah Road at 18:20:12, so the deviation was taken before and independently of any Pasir Panjang Road segment. An advisory on a road the recommended route never uses cannot satisfy POL-RD-23's requirement of an advisory that intersects the recommended route, and it cannot retrofit justification onto a departure already made.

The driver's 'AYE jam' is an uncorroborated assertion, and POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The only data for the AYE in the trip window (EV-ADVIS-05006-01) records no incident, roadwork or closure and speed bands 4-6 throughout, which is flowing traffic, not congestion. The rider's own account at filing was that the AYE looked clear past the slip road, which is consistent with the LTA record and not with the driver's claim.

The rider's 'ok' does not save the driver's case, and I do not overstate this: I accept that the driver messaged before the deviation (EV-CHAT-05006, MSG-05006-003 sent 18:01:46, 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?') and the rider replied 'ok' (MSG-05006-004, sent 18:02:11), while the deviation was detected at 18:05:06. POL-RD-21 makes that acknowledgment relevant only to whether the deviation is 'agreed'. POL-RD-24 row (a) yields no refund only where the reroute is traffic-justified as well as notified and agreed; a rider's agreement to a detour that the traffic record does not support does not make the detour traffic-justified. The driver therefore cannot bring himself within row (a), and rows (b) and (c), which also presuppose a traffic-justified reroute, are equally unavailable.

This case fits POL-RD-24 row (d) exactly: the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation was 1.90 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance. The consequence the policy attaches is refund of the excess distance fare in full, computed as deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd without surge: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD (EV-FARE-05006). That is precisely the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the present refund is the correct figure and the driver's claim to have the 1.37 SGD returned to his earnings is not supported by the matrix.

The outcome the rider is entitled to is PARTIAL_REFUND: part of the trip's charge — the excess distance fare — is returned, which is how POL-RD-24's own note labels rows (b) and (d), and it leaves the rider not carrying the charge for a 1.90 km detour the traffic record does not support. On the alternative reading, the present state already has the 1.37 SGD refunded (EV-FARE-05006: payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.37), and POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative — it preserves the present payment state and never restores a charge — so a NO_ACTION outcome would likewise leave the refund in the rider's hands rather than return the money to the driver. Either way the rider should not bear the disputed charge.

Nothing in this record requires escalation, and the rider's refund should be made terminal rather than held. The contested amount is 1.37 SGD (EV-FARE-05006, EV-TRIP-05006), below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence (value_band AI_FINAL) and POL-GEN-22's higher bars do not engage; POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied, and in any event the deviation is 1.90 km; and every fact the refund matrix needs — the two recorded distances, the notification and the acknowledgment in the chat log, and the traffic data — is in the record, with each artifact I rely on assessed COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 and POL-GEN-02 have no missing or impaired fact to bite on. There is no open question here for a human reviewer to answer.

The driver gave the rider notice of the deviation before the point of deviation, and the rider agreed. The chat log carries MSG-05006-003, sent by the driver at 18:01:46 — 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?' — read at 18:02:06, and the rider's reply MSG-05006-004 'ok' at 18:02:11, read by the driver at 18:02:35. The trip record places the first route_deviation_detected event at 18:05:06, and the driver-device trace still fixes the vehicle on the Ayer Rajah Expressway at 18:04:34, with the first West Coast Highway fix at 18:05:04. Under POL-RD-21 the acknowledgment in the chat log makes this an agreed deviation: the notification obligation the clause imposes was met before the deviation, not breached at it.

The rider's own account does not deny that notice was given; her complaint is only that the AYE 'looked clear to me' when they passed the slip road — an observation made from the slip road, that is at or after the 18:05:06 point of deviation, not at the moment the driver had to choose between staying on the expressway and taking West Coast Highway. The chat log shows four messages and no objection during the trip: the driver's contemporaneous in-writing report of the jam at 18:01:46, accepted in writing at 18:02:11. Nothing in the record contradicts the condition the driver reported at the time he had to act on it.

EV-ADVIS-05006-01 does not prove the AYE was flowing. Its type is NONE, and POL-RD-23's own admissible-type table places NONE outside the kinds that matter, so that artifact records the absence of an incident, a closure or a roadwork — it is not a congestion finding. No clause of this policy assigns any meaning to the speed-band figures the artifact carries, so those figures cannot be read as a finding that traffic was free-flowing. What POL-RD-23 excludes is a driver's bare assertion of traffic as justification; it does not convert a type-NONE record into affirmative evidence that the expressway was clear when the driver decided.

The traffic-justification question is not closed on this record. EV-ADVIS-05006-02 is a live ROADWORK — a 'closure' kind on POL-RD-23's admissible table — on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah near Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre, valid 09:00 to 23:00 on 18 August 2026 and so overlapping the trip window. The artifact's own derived facts leave justifies_reroute null and record the intersection with the recommended route as undetermined, to be decided by the Judge from its road, direction and location against the trip. POL-RD-23 turns on precisely that intersection, and the derived facts — which are the only licensed source for that comparison — do not determine it; the record therefore cannot establish that the reroute was not traffic-justified, which is the fact POL-RD-24's matrix rests on.

The case fits no row of POL-RD-24 cleanly. Rows (b) and (c) are excluded because the rider was informed and agreed, as the chat log shows. Row (a) — the only row written for an informed, agreeing rider — additionally requires the traffic justification to be established, and the advisories do not establish it. Rows (d) and (e) presuppose a settled finding that the reroute was not traffic-justified, which this record does not deliver. POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case which fits no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation where a fact a rule needs — here whether traffic justified the reroute — cannot be established. The interim SGD 1.37 should therefore be held for human review rather than confirmed against the driver. The driver does not dispute the measurement: 14.6 km minus 12.7 km is a 1.90 km deviation over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance; what is not established is the justification the refund turns on.

Confirming the full excess distance fare against the driver also overstates what the deviation cost the rider. The recommended route carried ERP of SGD 2.50 (EV-TRIP-05006, optimal_route_erp_sgd) while the trip actually charged ERP of SGD 1.50 (EV-FARE-05006, tolls_erp); on the route taken the rider was SGD 1.00 better off in tolls, so the net excess she bore was about SGD 0.37, not SGD 1.37. POL-RD-24's formula allows no set-off and the driver asks for none; the point goes to whether the interim recovery should be finalised on this record or held, as POL-RD-24's closing words and POL-GEN-26 direct, for a human reviewer.
